summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure (LVEF 20%), coronary artery disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obesity, was admitted for dyspnea and a 20-pound weight gain due to acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation, precipitated by medication noncompliance. He had stopped taking his diuretics and cardiac medications due to insurance and access issues. He was treated with IV furosemide, which improved his symptoms and reduced his weight to 130.8 kg. He experienced transient episodes of asymptomatic ventricular tachycardia, managed with ICD optimization and initiation of metoprolol. His kidney function temporarily worsened but improved with adjusted diuresis. He was discharged on home medications with spironolactone discontinued, hydralazine increased, and metoprolol started at 50 mg daily, with follow-up arranged to ensure medication access and ongoing management.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
Automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator in situ
Right bundle branch block and left anterior fascicular block
